# cpanel_email_filter (Resource)

Manages one ordered user-level cPanel email filter for an existing mailbox. For safety, actions are limited to `deliver`, `fail`, and `finish`; arbitrary file writes and command execution through `save` or `pipe` are rejected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cpanel_email_filter" "important" {
  account = "inbox@example.com"
  name    = "Important messages"
  enabled = true

  rules = [
    {
      part     = "$header_subject:"
      match    = "contains"
      value    = "[IMPORTANT]"
      operator = "none"
    },
  ]

  actions = [
    {
      action      = "deliver"
      destination = "archive@example.com"
    },
    {
      action      = "finish"
      destination = null
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account` (String) The existing mailbox that owns the user-level filter.
- `actions` (Attributes List) The ordered safe actions performed when the rules match. Only `deliver`, `fail`, and `finish` are supported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions))
- `name` (String) The cPanel filter name. Changing the name renames the filter in place.
- `rules` (Attributes List) The ordered conditions evaluated by cPanel. String and numeric comparisons are supported. Every rule except the last must use `and` or `or`; the last rule must use `none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether cPanel should evaluate the filter. Defaults to `true`.

<a id="nestedatt--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions`

Required:

- `action` (String) The action type: `deliver`, `fail`, or `finish`.

Optional:

- `destination` (String) The destination email address for `deliver` or rejection text for `fail`. Omit it for `finish`.


<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `match` (String) The comparison applied by the rule. Supported values are `is`, `matches`, `contains`, `does not contain`, `begins`, `does not begin`, `ends`, `does not end`, `does not match`, `is above`, `is not above`, `is below`, `is not below`, plus `none` for `not delivered` and `error_message`. Numeric comparisons require a base-10 integer value.
- `operator` (String) The connection to the next rule: `and`, `or`, or `none` for the final rule.
- `part` (String) The email section inspected by the rule. Supported canonical cPanel values are `$h_x-Spam-Bar:`, `$h_x-Spam-Score:`, `$h_X-Spam-Status:`, `$h_List-id:`, `$header_from:`, `$header_subject:`, `$header_to:`, `$reply_address:`, `$message_body`, `$message_headers`, `foranyaddress $h_to:,$h_cc:,$h_bcc:`, `not delivered`, `error_message`.
- `value` (String) The value matched by the rule. Use an empty string with `match = "none"` for `not delivered` and `error_message`. NUL, carriage return, and newline characters are rejected from other values.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cpanel_email_filter.important 'inbox@example.com|Important messages'
```
